scenes.tts: The nuclear pore is not a one-way door. So how can the same pore deliver one protein inward and another outward? Watch one pore between the cytoplasm and nucleus.
scenes.visual: Hook on the carried world immediately: a large cutaway fills the frame, cytoplasm left and nucleus right, separated by a double grey nuclear membrane. One central pore fills most of the frame height. Teal FG-repeat chains wave inside it. A yellow cargo drifts toward the pore from each side, then both stop under a bright question mark. Keep a small high-contrast SCHEMATIC label at top right. No title yet.
scenes.narration: The nuclear pore is not a one-way door. So how can the same pore deliver one protein inward and another outward? Watch one pore between the cytoplasm and nucleus.

scenes.visual: Keep the same cutaway moving gently. Dim it slightly and overlay the title ONE PORE, TWO DIRECTIONS for 1.5 seconds, then lift the overlay without changing the layout.

scenes.tts: Soluble cargo floats within either compartment instead of sitting in a membrane. Here is a first picture. For soluble protein cargo, the nuclear pore is a selective passage, not a one-way motor. Small grey particles slip between moving teal chains. Larger yellow cargo crosses slowly alone. Receptors engage the barrier for faster passage.
scenes.visual: In the same pore, animate several small grey dots weaving quickly between teal FG chains in both directions. A large yellow block tries alone and advances only slightly. A simple blue receptor shape then cups a second yellow block and threads through the waving chains. Show arrows in both directions, never a motor or piston. Keep SCHEMATIC visible.
scenes.narration: Soluble cargo floats within either compartment instead of sitting in a membrane. Here is a first picture. For soluble protein cargo, the nuclear pore is a selective passage, not a one-way motor. Small grey particles slip between moving teal chains. Larger yellow cargo crosses slowly alone. Receptors engage the barrier for faster passage.

scenes.tts: Cargo carries labels that transport-receptor proteins can read. A blue N L S tag recruits blue importin alpha, which holds cargo. Importin beta joins it and engages the pore. An orange N E S tag can recruit the purple export receptor C R M one.
scenes.caption: Cargo carries labels that transport-receptor proteins can read. A blue NLS tag recruits blue importin α, which holds cargo. Importin β joins it and engages the pore. An orange NES tag can recruit the purple export receptor CRM1.
scenes.visual: Hold the same cutaway. On the cytoplasmic left, a yellow cargo gains a small blue NLS tab; blue importin alpha and beta shapes close around it in two steps. On the nuclear right, a second yellow cargo gains an orange NES tab; a purple CRM1 crescent approaches but does not bind yet. Labels use at most NLS, importin, NES and CRM1.
scenes.narration: Cargo carries labels that transport-receptor proteins can read. A blue NLS tag recruits blue importin α, which holds cargo. Importin β joins it and engages the pore. An orange NES tag can recruit the purple export receptor CRM1.

scenes.tts: The difference between the two sides comes from Ran, a small switch protein. Ran is on with G T P and off with G D P. Green Ran G T P is abundant in the nucleus. Grey Ran G D P dominates in the cytoplasm. This unequal distribution is the Ran gradient.
scenes.caption: The difference between the two sides comes from Ran, a small switch protein. Ran is on with GTP and off with GDP. Green RanGTP is abundant in the nucleus. Grey RanGDP dominates in the cytoplasm. This unequal distribution is the Ran gradient.
scenes.visual: Zoom out slightly but keep the pore central. Green RanGTP tokens appear and drift throughout the nucleus; many grey RanGDP tokens drift in the cytoplasm. A fixed teal RCC1 station on chromatin changes one arriving grey token to green. A fixed teal RanGAP station outside changes one green token to grey. Keep the density difference obvious and label the whole distribution Ran gradient, schematic.
scenes.narration: The difference between the two sides comes from Ran, a small switch protein. Ran is on with GTP and off with GDP. Green RanGTP is abundant in the nucleus. Grey RanGDP dominates in the cytoplasm. This unequal distribution is the Ran gradient.

scenes.tts: In the simplest form, the import complex threads through the pore. It moves from cytoplasm to nucleus without a directional push. In the nucleus, green Ran G T P binds importin beta and separates it from importin alpha. Importin alpha then releases the blue-tagged cargo where Ran G T P is high. All three receptor and cargo pieces are now distinct.
scenes.caption: In the simplest form, the import complex threads through the pore. It moves from cytoplasm to nucleus without a directional push. In the nucleus, green RanGTP binds importin β and separates it from importin α. Importin α then releases the blue-tagged cargo where RanGTP is high. All three receptor and cargo pieces are now distinct.
scenes.visual: Carry the blue importin complex from the left through the central teal FG chains while the chains bend and rebound. Do not draw a pushing arrow. In the nucleus, one green RanGTP token clicks into importin beta; the two blue receptor pieces separate and the yellow NLS cargo drifts free. Leave the purple CRM1 and NES cargo waiting on the right.
scenes.narration: In the simplest form, the import complex threads through the pore. It moves from cytoplasm to nucleus without a directional push. In the nucleus, green RanGTP binds importin β and separates it from importin α. Importin α then releases the blue-tagged cargo where RanGTP is high. All three receptor and cargo pieces are now distinct.

scenes.tts: Now predict. If Ran G T P became equally common on both sides, could importin still unload only inside? Hold the two-sided picture in your mind.
scenes.caption: Now predict. If RanGTP became equally common on both sides, could importin still unload only inside? Hold the two-sided picture in your mind.
scenes.visual: Keep the full cutaway. Fade in matching green RanGTP densities on both sides while leaving one loaded blue importin complex near the pore. Put the question CAN IT UNLOAD ONLY INSIDE? across the top. Everything continues slow ambient motion.
scenes.narration: Now predict. If RanGTP became equally common on both sides, could importin still unload only inside? Hold the two-sided picture in your mind.

scenes.visual: Hold the prediction view for 4.5 seconds. Green RanGTP tokens drift on both sides, FG chains wave, and the loaded importin complex rocks gently. Keep the question visible; reveal no answer.

scenes.tts: No. Importin could still cross. But on either side, it might drop cargo or fail to pick it up. Net import would lose its one-sided rule. Restore the gradient, and cargo release again favors the nuclear side.
scenes.visual: With equal green tokens, show one importin dropping cargo in the cytoplasm and another failing to close around cargo there; replace the directional arrow with a two-headed grey arrow. Then sweep excess green tokens out of the cytoplasm toward RanGAP, restoring grey RanGDP outside. The nuclear release gains a bright check mark while the cytoplasmic failures fade.
scenes.narration: No. Importin could still cross. But on either side, it might drop cargo or fail to pick it up. Net import would lose its one-sided rule. Restore the gradient, and cargo release again favors the nuclear side.

scenes.tts: Export reverses the same rule. Nuclear green Ran G T P helps purple C R M one grip orange-tagged N E S cargo. The complex crosses outward. In the cytoplasm, Ran-binding proteins first help the cargo come free. Hydrolysis then turns Ran G T P into Ran G D P. This frees C R M one for another round.
scenes.caption: Export reverses the same rule. Nuclear green RanGTP helps purple CRM1 grip orange-tagged NES cargo. The complex crosses outward. In the cytoplasm, Ran-binding proteins first help the cargo come free. Hydrolysis then turns RanGTP into RanGDP. This frees CRM1 for another round.
scenes.visual: On the nuclear right, one green RanGTP token joins the waiting purple CRM1 and yellow NES cargo, closing the purple crescent around the cargo. Move the three-part complex through the same central FG chains to the cytoplasm. A small RanBP1 shape touches the complex and the cargo drifts free; only then does the green token turn grey at RanGAP and the purple crescent open.
scenes.narration: Export reverses the same rule. Nuclear green RanGTP helps purple CRM1 grip orange-tagged NES cargo. The complex crosses outward. In the cytoplasm, Ran-binding proteins first help the cargo come free. Hydrolysis then turns RanGTP into RanGDP. This frees CRM1 for another round.

scenes.tts: Nuclear Ran G T P tells importins to unload and exportins to load. Blue importins carry N L S cargo in. Purple C R M one carries many N E S cargoes out. One asymmetry gives opposite receptors useful directions.
scenes.caption: Nuclear RanGTP tells importins to unload and exportins to load. Blue importins carry NLS cargo in. Purple CRM1 carries many NES cargoes out. One asymmetry gives opposite receptors useful directions.
scenes.visual: Run import and export simultaneously through the one pore. Above it, the blue importin complex moves inward and opens beside green RanGTP. Below it, the purple CRM1 complex assembles beside green RanGTP and moves outward. Use two curved paths without collisions. A compact two-row key reads importin: unload and CRM1: load on the nuclear side.
scenes.narration: Nuclear RanGTP tells importins to unload and exportins to load. Blue importins carry NLS cargo in. Purple CRM1 carries many NES cargoes out. One asymmetry gives opposite receptors useful directions.

scenes.tts: In Ran-dependent protein transport, G T P hydrolysis maintains the gradient; it does not push cargo through the pore. In Ran-dependent transport, Ran mainly sets where cargo loads and unloads. Pore proteins still help on each face, but the pore sets no direction of its own. Most messenger R N A export uses another receptor.
scenes.caption: In Ran-dependent protein transport, GTP hydrolysis maintains the gradient; it does not push cargo through the pore. In Ran-dependent transport, Ran mainly sets where cargo loads and unloads. Pore proteins still help on each face, but the pore sets no direction of its own. Most messenger RNA export uses another receptor.
scenes.visual: Keep the complete world. Pulse the teal RCC1 and RanGAP stations as green tokens remain concentrated inside and grey tokens outside. Cross out a red piston icon beside the pore. Center the pore and the unequal Ran fields. Finish by briefly sending a grey RNA block outward on a separate dashed path labelled another receptor, without naming or detailing it.
scenes.narration: In Ran-dependent protein transport, GTP hydrolysis maintains the gradient; it does not push cargo through the pore. In Ran-dependent transport, Ran mainly sets where cargo loads and unloads. Pore proteins still help on each face, but the pore sets no direction of its own. Most messenger RNA export uses another receptor.

scenes.visual: End card over the still-moving cutaway. Large line: IN RAN-DEPENDENT TRANSPORT, RAN MAINLY SETS LOADING AND UNLOADING. Keep it on screen for 3.5 seconds with slow FG-chain and Ran-token motion.
